candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — positioning, mobility, and prevention of complications from immobility
candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — perioperative positioning safety
candidate.educational_objective: Use padding, alignment, appropriate positioning devices, and ongoing reassessment to reduce perioperative positioning injury.

options.A: Use appropriate positioning devices, pad vulnerable bony prominences, maintain alignment, and reassess positioning throughout the case for pressure or alignment problems.
options.B: Position the client once before incision and avoid further reassessment unless the surgeon specifically requests it.
options.C: Use improvised rolled towels or fluid bags instead of approved positioning equipment whenever standard devices are not immediately available.
options.D: Prioritize operating-room turnover efficiency over the final positioning safety check because prolonged setup increases risk more than malposition.

candidate.rationale: AORN positioning guidance emphasizes appropriate positioning devices, padding of bony prominences, alignment, and reassessment during the case. Prolonged immobility increases positioning and pressure-injury risk, so a one-time setup is insufficient and improvised unsafe supports or skipped checks are not appropriate substitutes.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Perioperative nurses should use appropriate positioning/padding, maintain alignment, and reassess positioning for pressure and alignment concerns throughout the case.
candidate.source_document_title: Feeling Rushed? 5 Patient Positioning Checks to Keep Patients Safe
candidate.source_locator: 4. For frontline RNs: Make Time To Reassess Positioning
candidate.stem: During a prolonged surgical procedure, which perioperative nursing action best reduces positioning-related injury risk?
